start: If I experience any of the following warning signs
end: in the second half of pregnancy)
note: Includes the form instruction "Put a check (✔)." "Watery vaginal discharge" mapped to water breaking is an interpretation: please confirm or drop it.
body:
If I experience any of the following warning signs, I should
immediately seek consultation at a health facility. Put a check (✔).
Swelling of the legs, hands and/or face
Severe headache, dizziness, blurring of vision
Vaginal bleeding
Pallor or anemia
Fever and chills
Vomiting
Fast or difficult breathing
Severe abdominal pain
Vaginal discharge
Painful urination
Watery vaginal discharge
Convulsions
Absence of/or reduced fetal movements
(less than 10 kicks in 12 hours in the
second half of pregnancy)

start: When to seek care on danger signs
note: WHO's "go now, day or night" list for pregnancy. "Fever and too weak to get out of bed" as looks_very_ill is an interpretation.
body:
When to seek care on danger signs
Go to the hospital or health centre immediately, day or night, DO NOT wait, if any of the
following signs:
vaginal bleeding
convulsions/fits
severe headaches with blurred vision
fever and too weak to get out of bed
severe abdominal pain
fast or difficult breathing.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

start: Go to the health centre as soon as possible
note: WHO's second level: "as soon as possible", not "immediately". Liora has only go-now and calm today: see question 1.
body:
Go to the health centre as soon as possible if any of the following signs:
fever
abdominal pain
water breaks and not in labour after 6 hours
feel ill
swollen fingers, face and legs.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

note: Signs of labour, with the 12-hour rule.
body:
Know the signs of labour
If you have any of these signs, go to the health centre as soon as you can.
If these signs continue for 12 hours or more, you need to go immediately.
Painful contractions every 20 minutes or less.
Bag of water breaks.
Bloody sticky discharge.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

start: Visit the health centre at least 4 times
body: Visit the health centre at least 4 times during your pregnancy, even if you do not have any problems.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

start: If at any time you have any concerns
note: Calm answer, and a good general fallback.
body: If at any time you have any concerns about your or your baby’s health, go to the health centre.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

body: Do not take medication unless prescribed at the health centre.

start: When to seek care for danger signs
end: shortness of breath or chest pain.
note: WHO's "go now" list after birth: the source the postpartum rules were waiting for.
body:
When to seek care for danger signs
Go to hospital or health centre immediately, day or night, DO NOT wait, if any of the following signs:
Vaginal bleeding has increased.
Fits.
Fast or difficult breathing.
Fever and too weak to get out of bed.
Severe headaches with blurred vision.
Calf pain, redness or swelling; shortness of breath or chest pain.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

start: Go to health centre as soon as possible
note: Second level after birth: see question 1.
body:
Go to health centre as soon as possible if any of the following signs:
Swollen, red or tender breasts or nipples.
Problems urinating, or leaking.
Increased pain or infection in the perineum.
Infection in the area of the wound.
Smelly vaginal discharge.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

body:
Wash all over daily, particularly the perineum.
Change pad every 4 to 6 hours. Wash pad or dispose of it safely.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

body:
Rest when you can.
Drink plenty of clean, safe water.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

start: If you or your baby has any of these signs
note: Heading of the delivery danger-sign box; pairs with the next card. In the PDF they sit in one box: please check the page.
body:
If you or your baby has any of these signs, go to the hospital or health centre immediately,
day or night, Do not wait.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition

start: If waters break and not in labour
note: The mother's signs from that box.
body:
If waters break and not in labour after 6 hours.
Labour pains (contractions) continue for more than 12 hours.
Heavy bleeding (soaks more than 2-3 pads in 15 minutes).
Placenta not expelled 1 hour after birth of baby.

citation.title: Pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum and newborn care: a guide for essential practice, 3rd edition
